title: Degradation choropleth and tracehook integration playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a reproducible playbook and dashboard pattern that maps multidimensional degradation signals onto a choropleth-style view (service/region/queue) and wires tracehook annotations to metric/log pipelines. Goal: help SREs and oncall quickly localize root cause across timeouts, overload, model rejections, and transport errors (HTTP/gRPC codes). This work bundles a dashboard template, tracehook schema recommendations, metrics enrichment pipeline changes, and runbook snippets for incident response.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard template deployed to Console showing choropleth by service/region/instance with selectable failure-type overlay (timeouts, overload, model_errors, http_grpc_codes)
Tracehook annotation schema documented and accepted by runtime team (fields, sample-rate, span-tags) and wired into tracecollector to enrich error signals
Metrics/log pipeline enrichment implemented to attach trace IDs, failure_category, and model_variant tags at emit time for top 10 high-volume services
Runbook section with 4 guided playbook steps (isolate region, check queue/backpressure, inspect model rejection slices, validate transport code distribution) added to oncall docs
E2E test that injects synthetic timeouts and model rejection events and verifies the choropleth highlights the affected zone within 30s of injection
implementation_notes: Use existing tracehook SDK v0.9.2 but extend annotation types with 'failure_category' and 'model_variant' tags
Choropleth will be implemented as heatmap matrix in Console using service x region grid; use percent-of-requests failing and p95 latency color scaling
Metric enrichment will add 'failure_category' label to the aggregation rollups; keep cardinality limited to allowed set [timeout, overload, model_error, transport_error]
Log pipeline (fluentd) filter stage to attach canonical_failure and trace_id if present; follow retention and PII rules
Tradeoffs: adding tags increases metric cardinality and cost — mitigate via low-cardinality canonical tags + optional high-cardinality model_variant only for sampling-enabled routes
progress_updates: 2026-02-14: Kickoff meeting with runtime, console, and ingest teams. Aligned on primary failure taxonomy and initial UI wireframe.
2026-02-20: Prototype wireframe uploaded. Design requested alternate color ramp and explicit legend for p95 vs error-rate overlays (see docs link).
2026-02-26: Runtime agreed to add 'failure_category' tag to tracehook API; PR for SDK changes opened by runtime: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1874

2026-03-02: Ingest engineers proposed sampling strategy to avoid metric explosion — default 5% model_variant, 100% for failure_category. Decision: accept sampling plan with opt-in per-service override.
2026-03-05: Console heatmap component prototype renders synthetic data locally. Need backend endpoint to serve aggregated choropleth tiles.
2026-03-07: Began implementing fluentd filter and metrics enrichment rule; created branch infra/observability/choropleth-enrichments
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Metric cardinality blowup increases cost. Mitigation: limit canonical tags and apply sampling for high-cardinality model_variant.
Risk: Tracehook adoption lag across services. Mitigation: provide lightweight helper library and a one-day migration support window with runtime team.
Risk: UI misinterpretation of choropleth colors. Mitigation: explicit legend, tooltips with raw numbers, and a toggle between rate and absolute counts.
runbook_snippets: Step 1: If choropleth shows a spike in 'timeout' for region eu-west-1 -> check node autoscaler and GPU queue length metric 'gpu.queue.length'
Step 2: If 'model_error' concentrated on a single model_variant -> pin traffic to previous stable variant and file model-regression ticket with Research
Step 3: If transport_error high and HTTP 503/504 dominate -> validate ingress LB health and upstream capacity, escalate to infra
Step 4: Use console trace lookup with failure_category tag to pull sample spans and run local flamegraphs
